job.title: Finance Assistant
job.description:

This is a rare chance to join an industry leader and be part of a finance team that gets the work done so people can actually enjoy their evenings. You’ll work hard, hit deadlines, and then switch off – and you won’t be expected to take yourself too seriously along the way.
As Finance Assistant you’ll sit across payables, payroll and receivables, so you’ll build breadth rather than being locked into a single ledger. You’ll also have a genuine mandate to look at how the work is done – tightening processes and exploring where AI and smarter tools can take the grind out of the day.
This is an office-based role on Moorhouse Avenue in a modern workspace just steps from local cafés, gyms and lunch spots. You get the convenience of central Christchurch without the CBD traffic.

The Company
Harcourts is the largest real estate brand in New Zealand. Grenadier Real Estate Limited is the largest Harcourts franchise in the South Island – known for exemplary service and a habit of delivering above and beyond its competitors.
The business now employs more than 260 people across 10 office locations. You’ll join a finance team that values teamwork, good-hearted humour and getting the job done without the fuss. It’s a stable, well-known brand with the scale to keep you busy and the culture to make the work enjoyable.

The Role
You’ll be a key part of the finance team. The role has a payables and payroll focus, but you’ll work interchangeably across the team so deadlines are met. Duties include:
  • End-to-end processing of accounts payable
  • Processing payroll, resolving queries and posting journals
  • Supporting accounts receivable processing
  • Reconciliations and ad hoc finance administration
  • Identifying process improvements and helping develop practical AI and automation solutions that make finance workflows faster, cleaner and less manual
Your Profile
You’re organised, methodical and happy to multi-task. You’ll bring:
  • Existing and valid New Zealand working rights (sponsorship is not offered)

  • Curiosity about better ways of working – comfortable spotting process gaps and open to using AI and digital tools to improve how finance gets done
  • Full working rights are required and no sponsorship is offered.

job.title: Project Accountant
job.description:
The Opportunity
You’re a project accountant who likes being useful - not just closing the books. You want a role where month-end still matters, but so does sitting with project managers, understanding what’s happening on their jobs, and explaining the numbers in plain language.

Based in Christchurch and reporting to the Finance Manager, you’ll look after the integrity of the financial accounts and help keep month-end accurate and on time. You’ll review journals, reconciliations and work prepared by others, support fixed assets, leases, GST, FBT and income tax, and play a visible part in year-end and audit. Just as important, you’ll build real working relationships with project managers - reviewing revenue, costs, accruals and margins, and helping them understand performance, risk and forecast outcomes rather than reporting the numbers after the fact.

Over the next 12 months a key part of the role is developing the finance team. Processes are being shared more widely, and you’ll train, coach and review others so the team has more depth and can operate with less reliance on any one person. If you enjoy lifting people as well as lifting the quality of the numbers, this is a role that will use both sides of how you work.

The Company
You’ll join a well-established Christchurch business that delivers solutions for clients across New Zealand. Work is project-based, so finance sits close to delivery - supporting project managers, keeping commercial information current, and helping the business see performance early enough to act. 

The Role
You’ll keep the accounts sound and make the numbers useful to the people delivering the work. Key responsibilities include:
  • Review project revenue, costs, accruals, margins and financial position; challenge unusual movements and help project managers understand the commercial story behind their results
  • Support project revenue recognition and month-end project accounting, and give practical financial advice to project managers and operational leader. 
  • Support an accurate, timely month-end close — maintain general ledger integrity, prepare and review balance sheet reconciliations, journals, accruals and adjustments
  • Support accounting for fixed assets, depreciation, capital work in progress, leases and other month-end adjustments, and assist with GST, FBT, income tax, year-end reporting and external audit
  • Build trusted working relationships with project managers; join regular project financial reviews and develop a clear view of performance, risks, opportunities and forecast outcomes
  • (Once up to speed) Coach and train finance team members across accounting and month-end processes, review their work, explain the principles behind the tasks, and act as an escalation point for more complex transactions
Your Profile
Technical accounting ability matters here - but so does how you work with people. You’ll bring:
  • Ideally, strong financial or project accounting experience, a sound grasp of accounting principles, and proven month-end, reconciliation and general ledger review skills - including confidence reviewing the work of others
  • Excellent communication and relationship skills; you’re comfortable working with project managers and other non-finance stakeholders, and can explain accounting clearly without talking down. 
  • Strong Excel skills, confidence in financial systems (MYOB experience is useful), and the ability to manage competing priorities in a busy project environment
  • Ideally, experience in construction, engineering, infrastructure or another project-based industry, including long-term contracts, margins, variations and revenue recognition; CA/CPA (or working towards) is highly regarded

job.title: Chief Financial Officer

The Opportunity
This is a broad finance leadership role within a business that wants finance to play a bigger part in where it goes next.
  
Working alongside the leadership team, you’ll bring greater commercial focus to planning, performance and decision-making across the organisation. Rather than simply reporting on what has already happened, you’ll help the business understand what is driving its results, where the opportunities sit and what may need to change.
  
There is still a hands-on element to the position. You’ll have oversight of the core finance function and will need to be comfortable moving between strategic conversations, commercial analysis and the practical realities of running finance in a busy organisation.
  
It’s a role with genuine breadth and visibility, offering the opportunity to influence business direction while remaining closely connected to operational performance and financial delivery.

You’ll be joining an established New Zealand organisation with a solid foundation and a clear appetite to keep improving.
  
The working environment is practical, collaborative and relatively down to earth. People are encouraged to contribute beyond their immediate area, and the leadership team values straightforward advice backed by good information.
  
Finance is seen as an important part of the business rather than simply a reporting function. The opportunity is to build on what is already in place, bring a sharper commercial lens and help shape how the organisation approaches future decisions.
  
The Role
  • Work alongside the leadership team on business priorities, future plans and key commercial decisions
  • Bring greater visibility to the factors driving revenue, margin, costs and overall performance
  • Lead annual planning and regular forecasting, giving the business a realistic view of what lies ahead
  • Build models and business cases around investment, pricing, growth opportunities and operational change
  • Turn financial and operational information into clear recommendations that leaders can act on
  • Ask the right questions, test assumptions and provide constructive challenge when decisions are being made
  • Maintain close oversight of cashflow, working capital and the organisation’s wider financial position
  • Oversee management and statutory reporting, controls, compliance and relationships with external advisors
  • Improve the quality, speed and usefulness of reporting across the business
  • Lead a compact and dynamic team and create the capacity for finance to contribute more widely
  
Your Profile
  • A strong background in broad senior finance roles, with experience contributing beyond the traditional reporting and control remit
  • A recognised accounting qualification, supported by sound experience across financial management and commercial decision support
  • The judgement and confidence to contribute meaningfully alongside senior leaders
  • Strong forecasting, modelling and analytical skills, with the ability to identify the commercial story behind the numbers
  • Experience contributing to pricing, investment decisions, business cases, profitability or performance improvement
